description: Check whether a PR is ready to merge, tell the user its status, and if ready, ask whether to merge it.

evals.name: Step 7: gh pr merge --delete-branch exits non-zero, state is MERGED, remote branch still present
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/API calls -- describe exactly what you would do instead, and write your answer to a file.

You are at step 7 of your own procedure. `merge_auto_delete_branch` is `true`. You ran `gh pr merge 142 --rebase --delete-branch`; it exited non-zero with local stderr `fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree '/repo'`. You then check `gh pr view 142 --json state,mergeCommit` and confirm `state` is `MERGED`. `headRefName` (from step 1) is `feat/some-feature`.

Describe every check you perform next, in order, and what you do if the remote branch turns out to still exist. Write your answer to `outputs/procedure.md`.
evals.expected_output: Does not report this as a merge failure (state is MERGED). Explicitly runs `git ls-remote --heads origin feat/some-feature` to check whether the remote branch actually still exists, rather than assuming the local error means the whole `--delete-branch` operation failed or assuming it silently succeeded anyway. If that check comes back non-empty, validates `headRefName` against `^[A-Za-z0-9._/@+=-]+$` and then completes the deletion via `gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/feat/some-feature`. Reports plainly that this fallback ran.

evals.name: Step 5: worktree branch-delete note is present regardless of merge_auto_delete_branch
evals.prompt: This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT actually call AskUserQuestion -- instead, describe exactly what you would ask and what it would say. Given `MERGE ALLOWED` and full readiness at step 5, describe the exact content of the confirmation prompt you present via AskUserQuestion, including any notes about possible local git errors. Write your answer to `outputs/prompt.md`. Do this without knowing what `merge_auto_delete_branch` is set to (it isn't read until a later step).
evals.expected_output: Includes a note that branch deletion may report a local git error (something like `fatal: '<default>' is already used by worktree ...`) even though the merge itself succeeds, and that this is expected/handled automatically -- and states this note is present unconditionally, not gated on `merge_auto_delete_branch`, since that setting isn't read until step 6 (after step 5 already ran).

evals.name: headRefName validated at step 1, before any shell interpolation
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- describe exactly what you would do instead.

You are following your own step 1. `gh pr view $ARGUMENTS --json number,isDraft,headRefName,files,reviews,statusCheckRollup` returns `headRefName: "feat/x;rm -rf /"` (a maliciously crafted branch name containing a shell metacharacter). Describe every check you perform, in order, and what happens next -- specifically, do you ever reach step 7's `git ls-remote` call with this value?
evals.expected_output: Validates headRefName against ^[A-Za-z0-9._/@+=-]+$ immediately at step 1, before any other step. The value `feat/x;rm -rf /` fails this regex (contains `;` and space). Stops immediately and tells the user -- never proceeds to step 7's git ls-remote or any other use of headRefName.

evals.name: Fork PR: remote-branch-deletion fallback skipped when isCrossRepository is true
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- describe exactly what you would do instead.

You are at step 7. `merge_auto_delete_branch` is `true`. `isCrossRepository` (from step 1) is `true` -- this PR came from a contributor's fork, not a branch of this repository. You ran `gh pr merge 150 --rebase --delete-branch`; it exited non-zero with local stderr `fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree '/repo'`. You then check `gh pr view 150 --json state,mergeCommit` and confirm `state` is `MERGED`.

Describe every check you perform next, and specifically: do you ever run `git ls-remote --heads origin <headRefName>` or `gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/<branch>` in this scenario? Why or why not?
evals.expected_output: Never runs git ls-remote or gh api -X DELETE for this PR, because isCrossRepository is true -- {owner}/{repo} in this skill's own repo-scoped grants would resolve to this repository, not the fork the branch actually lives in. Reports that the branch lives in the contributor's fork and isn't this skill's to delete. Does not attempt to determine or guess the fork's own owner/repo to retarget the deletion -- simply skips the fallback and reports plainly.

evals.name: Step 7: gh pr merge --delete-branch exits 0 but the remote branch silently remains
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- describe exactly what you would do instead.

You are at step 7. `merge_auto_delete_branch` is `true`. `isCrossRepository` (from step 1) is `false`. You ran `gh pr merge 160 --rebase --delete-branch`; it exited 0 (success, no error at all). Per your own step 7, what do you check next? Specifically: do you ever run `git ls-remote --heads origin <headRefName>` in this scenario, given the merge command itself reported success with no error? If that check came back non-empty (the branch is still on the remote despite the clean exit), what would you do?
evals.expected_output: States it checks gh pr view --json state,mergeCommit regardless of the merge command's exit code, then -- since merge_auto_delete_branch is true and isCrossRepository is false -- always runs git ls-remote --heads origin <headRefName>, explicitly stating this runs even though the merge command exited 0 with no error. Does not skip or treat the ls-remote check as conditional on a prior non-zero exit. If asked what happens on non-empty output: states it completes the deletion via gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/<branch>, the same fallback used in the non-zero-exit case.

evals.name: headRefName allowlist accepts Git-valid, shell-safe characters but still rejects shell metacharacters
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- describe exactly what you would do instead.

You are following your own step 1. `gh pr view $ARGUMENTS --json ...` returns three different PRs' `headRefName` values, one at a time: (a) `feature+api`, (b) `user@topic/release=next`, (c) `feat/x;rm -rf /`. For each, state whether it passes your headRefName validation regex, and if it doesn't, what happens next.
evals.expected_output: States (a) feature+api passes validation. States (b) user@topic/release=next passes validation. States (c) feat/x;rm -rf / fails validation (contains ; and a space, neither in the allowlist) and the skill stops and tells the user rather than proceeding to any later use of headRefName. Does not reject (a) or (b) -- explicitly names @, +, and = as characters the current regex admits, distinct from the shell metacharacters (c) is rejected for.

evals.name: Step 2: four-state CI classification distinguishes missing from pending
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/API calls -- you are given the data those calls would have returned, as facts for this exercise. Describe what you would conclude and do, and write your answer to a file.

You are at step 2. The base branch's required-check list (from the branchProtectionRule GraphQL query) is: `Hygiene (PR contract)`, `Python quality (ruff, ty, pytest)`, `Fork PR (unsupported)`, `Publish Codex policy result`. Step 1's `statusCheckRollup` (already fetched) contains exactly these three entries: a `CheckRun` named `Hygiene (PR contract)` with `status: COMPLETED, conclusion: SUCCESS`; a `CheckRun` named `Python quality (ruff, ty, pytest)` with `status: IN_PROGRESS`; a `CheckRun` named `Publish Codex policy result` with `status: COMPLETED, conclusion: SUCCESS`. Note that `Fork PR (unsupported)` has no matching entry in `statusCheckRollup` at all. Classify each of the 4 required contexts into exactly one state, and state whether this PR is ready to merge. Write your answer to `outputs/answer.md`.
evals.expected_output: Classifies Hygiene (PR contract) as passing, Python quality as pending, Publish Codex policy result as passing, and Fork PR (unsupported) as missing (not pending, not failing) -- explicitly noting missing means no run was ever recorded for the current head commit, which is distinct from pending (a run exists but hasn't finished). Concludes the PR is not ready to merge, since not every required context classifies as passing.

evals.name: Step 7(a): rebase-compatibility pre-check fires before attempting --rebase
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- you are given the data those calls would have returned, as facts for this exercise. Describe what you would do, and write your answer to a file.

You are at step 7. `pr_merge_type` (from step 6) is `REBASE`. You are given, as a fact for this exercise, that `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<number>/commits --paginate --jq '.[] | select((.parents | length) > 1) | .sha'` would return exactly one SHA. Before you would ever call `gh pr merge <n> --rebase`, what do you do? Write your answer to `outputs/answer.md`.
evals.expected_output: States it runs the merge-commit count check first, given the pr_merge_type is REBASE, and finds the count is 1 (non-zero). Tells the user the branch contains 1 merge commit and that --rebase will be rejected by GitHub. Asks via AskUserQuestion which alternate strategy to use (Merge or Squash) before ever attempting gh pr merge --rebase -- does not wait for a live rejection from the --rebase call itself.

evals.name: Step 7(c): squash tradeoff discloses even when SQUASH is the configured default from the start
evals.prompt:
This is a simulated exercise: there is no real GitHub PR to operate on, and you must NOT attempt any `gh`/`git` calls -- you are given the data those calls would have returned, as facts for this exercise. Describe what you would do, and write your answer to a file.

You are at step 7. `pr_merge_type` (from step 6) is `SQUASH` -- this was the configured setting from the start, not a strategy chosen via the rebase pre-check or a rejection fallback. You are given, as a fact for this exercise, that this PR has 12 commits. Before you run `gh pr merge <n> --squash`, what do you do? Write your answer to `outputs/answer.md`.
evals.expected_output: States that the squash-tradeoff disclosure still fires, even though SQUASH was already the configured pr_merge_type and no rebase pre-check or fallback was involved -- explicitly notes this isn't conditioned on having reached squash via a fallback path. States the number of commits that will collapse into one (12) and that individual fix-round/review-commit granularity will be lost on the base branch. States this disclosure happens before the --squash merge command runs.
